countries.name: Switzerland
countries.lead: Glaciers, car-free villages and the classic resorts of the Swiss Alps.

countries.name: Austria
countries.lead: Tyrol and the Arlberg: old ski towns, big ski areas and quiet high plateaus.

countries.name: France
countries.lead: Chalet villages below Mont Blanc and the high slopes of Les 3 Vallées.

countries.name: Italy
countries.lead: The Dolomites: big views, long lunches and skiing between the peaks.

countries.name: Germany
countries.lead: The Zugspitze, the Berchtesgaden Alps, and Munich for a city night before or after the snow.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.lead: Las Leñas, in the Andes of Mendoza, for the southern winter: where our founder, Juan Rodrigo, grew up skiing.

places.name: St. Moritz

image.alt: St. Moritz and its grand hotels above the frozen lake

places.tagline: The sunny high valley of the Engadin, host of two Winter Olympics.
places.intro: St. Moritz lies at about 1,800 m in the Upper Engadin, with Corviglia above the village and a frozen lake below it in deep winter.
facts: Zurich (about 3 hours); Engadin Airport in Samedan for private flights
Skiing with style, winter events on the lake
places.who: Guests who want classic grand hotels, sunny pistes and a winter calendar full of events.
places.when: Winter for skiing and the events on the frozen lake; summer for hiking, biking and the Engadin lakes.
places.how: About three hours from Zurich by car or train. Private flights land at Engadin Airport in Samedan, a few minutes away.

places.name: Zermatt

image.alt: Zermatt's chalets at dusk below the Matterhorn

places.tagline: A car-free village below the Matterhorn, skiing over into Italy.
places.intro: Zermatt is a car-free village in the Valais below the Matterhorn, 4,478 m. Its ski area reaches the Matterhorn Glacier Paradise and links over the border to Cervinia.
facts: By train from Täsch or Visp; cars stay in Täsch
High-altitude skiing, mountaineering, a long season
places.who: Skiers who want altitude and long runs, and mountaineers drawn by the Matterhorn and the high peaks around it.
places.when: Winter for skiing on both sides of the border; summer for glacier skiing, hiking and mountaineering.
places.how: By train to Visp, then the mountain railway to Zermatt. Drivers leave the car in Täsch and take the shuttle train for the last few minutes.

places.name: Laax

image.alt: The village of Laax and its church in winter, below snow-covered mountains

places.tagline: A big ski area with five snow parks and the largest halfpipe in the world.
places.intro: The LAAX ski area reaches from 1,100 m up to 3,018 m on the Vorab Glacier, with 216 km of slopes and 30 lifts, and is reached from Flims, Laax and Falera.
facts: Five snow parks and the largest halfpipe in the world
Arranged by us, ready to collect at the ticket desks in Flims, Laax and Falera
places.who: Skiers and snowboarders of every level, from children to adults, and freestyle riders who come for the snow parks and the halfpipe.
places.when: Winter for skiing, the snow parks, sledging, ice skating and cross-country skiing; summer for biking, hiking, river rafting and the Rhine Gorge.
places.how: About 30 minutes by car from Chur. By train to Chur, then about 30 minutes by PostBus; or from Chur by the Rhaetian Railway through the Rhine Gorge to Ilanz, and on by PostBus. [laax.com](https://www.laax.com/en)

places.name: Gstaad

image.alt: Snow-covered chalets in Gstaad, with the Gstaad Palace and the mountains behind

places.tagline: A car-free promenade, chalets, and the high skiing of Glacier 3000.
places.intro: Gstaad is a chalet village in the Saanenland, known for its pedestrian promenade, its hotels and the high-alpine skiing of Glacier 3000.
facts: Geneva (about 2 hours), Bern (about 1.5 hours); Saanen airfield for private flights
places.who: Families and couples who want a calm village, beautiful chalets and skiing at their own pace.
places.when: Winter for skiing; summer for hiking, festivals and tennis.
places.how: About two hours from Geneva Airport by car, or by train via Montreux on the scenic GoldenPass line.

places.name: Engelberg

image.alt: The Titlis above the Engelberg valley in winter

places.tagline: A monastery village below the Titlis glacier, under an hour from Lucerne.
places.intro: Engelberg grew up around its Benedictine monastery, founded in 1120. Above the village, lifts climb to the Titlis glacier at over 3,000 m.
places.who: Strong skiers looking for freeride terrain, and families who want an easy trip from Zurich or Lucerne.
places.when: Winter for skiing, with the Titlis glacier often holding snow late into spring; summer for hiking and the mountain lakes.
places.how: About an hour and a half from Zurich Airport by car or train. Lucerne is under an hour away.

places.name: Lech am Arlberg

image.alt: Lech am Arlberg under deep snow

places.tagline: High, snow-sure and quiet: Lech, Zürs, Zug and Oberlech on the Arlberg.
places.intro: Lech is a village in Vorarlberg on the Arlberg. It is part of Ski Arlberg, one of the largest connected ski areas in Austria, with Zürs, St. Anton and Warth-Schröcken on the same lift pass.
facts: Ski Arlberg: Lech, Zürs, Zug, Oberlech, St. Anton, Stuben, Warth-Schröcken
Ski weeks with excellent food and hotels; off-piste with a guide
places.who: Skiers who want big terrain without big crowds, and families who want to ski from a small village.
places.when: Winter for skiing, usually from early December to late April. Summer for hiking in the Lech valley.
places.how: Innsbruck Airport is about an hour and a half away by car; Zurich about two and a half hours. By train to Langen am Arlberg or St. Anton, then a short transfer.

places.name: Kitzbühel

image.alt: Kitzbühel under snow, seen from the north-west

places.tagline: A medieval town, and the Hahnenkamm with its famous Streif.
places.intro: Kitzbühel combines a walled old town with one of Austria's best-known ski areas and the Streif, the downhill of the Hahnenkamm races each January.
facts: Salzburg or Innsbruck (about 1¼ hours), Munich (about 2 hours)
Skiing with town life, the Hahnenkamm weekend, golf in summer
places.who: Skiers who want lively evenings in town after the slopes, and couples and families who like long, cruising runs.
places.when: Winter for skiing and the Hahnenkamm races in January; summer for golf, hiking and biking.
places.how: Salzburg and Innsbruck airports are each about an hour and a quarter away by car; Munich Airport about two hours.

places.name: Seefeld in Tirol

image.alt: A floodlit cross-country trail leading to the Seekirchl in Seefeld

places.tagline: A sunny high plateau above Innsbruck, made for cross-country skiing.
places.intro: Seefeld sits on a plateau at about 1,200 m, half an hour above Innsbruck. It hosted the Nordic events of the 1964 and 1976 Winter Olympics and the 2019 Nordic World Ski Championships.
facts: Rosshütte and Gschwandtkopf, and long cross-country trails
Cross-country skiing, families, wellness, gentle skiing
places.who: Families, cross-country skiers and anyone who wants a quieter week with spa days, winter walks and easy skiing.
places.when: Winter for cross-country and downhill skiing; summer for hiking, biking and golf on the plateau.
places.how: Innsbruck Airport is about 30 minutes away by car. Seefeld also has its own station on the railway from Innsbruck to Garmisch-Partenkirchen.

places.name: Innsbruck

image.alt: The colourful houses of Mariahilf on the Inn, with the snow-covered Nordkette above Innsbruck

places.tagline: A city in the mountains, twice host of the Winter Olympics.
places.intro: The capital of Tyrol has the Nordkette range right above its old town and several ski areas within half an hour's drive.
facts: Innsbruck (INN), about 15 minutes from the centre
Short breaks, city and skiing in one trip
places.who: Guests who want a city and the mountains in the same day: a cable car from the old town to the Nordkette, and a different ski area every day.
places.when: Winter for skiing in the surrounding areas; summer for hiking and biking straight from town.
places.how: Innsbruck Airport is just outside the city. Munich Airport is about two hours by car, and Innsbruck is a main stop on the train line between Munich and Italy.

places.name: Megève

image.alt: Megève below the snowy slopes, with the Mont Blanc massif behind

places.tagline: A village of chalets with views of Mont Blanc, about an hour from Geneva.
places.intro: Megève was developed as a ski resort in the 1920s by the Rothschild family and has kept the feel of a Savoyard village: stone streets, chalets and wide, tree-lined slopes.
places.who: Families and groups who want a private chalet, gentle and scenic skiing, and a village with good restaurants.
places.when: Winter for skiing and the village at Christmas; summer for hiking, biking and golf with views of Mont Blanc.
places.how: About an hour and a quarter from Geneva Airport by car. By train to Sallanches, then about 20 minutes by road.

places.name: Courchevel

image.alt: Courchevel's hotels at the foot of the ski slopes

places.tagline: The top of Les 3 Vallées, with its own altiport.
places.intro: Courchevel is a set of villages at the top of Les 3 Vallées, one of the largest linked ski areas in the world, which also includes Méribel and Val Thorens.
facts: Geneva or Lyon (about 2.5 hours), Chambéry (about 1.5 hours); the altiport for small aircraft and helicopters
places.who: Skiers who want a different valley every day, and groups who want a chalet with a chef.
places.when: Winter, usually from December to April.
places.how: By car from Geneva or Lyon in about two and a half hours, or by train to Moûtiers and then about 40 minutes by road. Helicopter and small-plane transfers land at the altiport.

places.name: Cortina d'Ampezzo

image.alt: Cortina d'Ampezzo under fresh snow at dawn, with the Dolomites behind

places.tagline: The Dolomites, host of the Winter Olympics in 1956 and 2026.
places.intro: Cortina d'Ampezzo sits in a wide valley ringed by the Dolomites, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It hosted the 1956 Winter Olympics and co-hosted the Winter Olympics of 2026 with Milan.
facts: Skiing with views, long lunches, ski touring
places.who: Skiers who care as much about the view and the lunch as the run, and couples who want an Italian mountain town.
places.when: Winter for skiing; summer for hiking, via ferrata and the high passes of the Dolomites.
places.how: About two hours by car from Venice Airport or Innsbruck Airport.

places.name: Berchtesgaden

image.alt: St. Bartholomä on Lake Königssee below the east face of the Watzmann

places.tagline: A national park, Lake Königssee and the Watzmann, on the border with Salzburg.
places.intro: In the far south-east corner of Germany, Berchtesgaden is surrounded by the Berchtesgaden Alps and by Germany's only national park in the Alps.
facts: Lake Königssee and the Watzmann, 2,713 m
Families, winter walks, tobogganing, a quieter ski week
places.who: Families and couples who want winter beyond the piste: walks, tobogganing, cross-country and spa days, with skiing close by in Germany and Austria.
places.when: Winter for snow and Christmas in the mountains. Late spring to autumn for hiking, the lake and e-bike tours.
places.how: Salzburg Airport is about 40 minutes away by car; Munich Airport about two hours.

places.name: Garmisch-Partenkirchen

image.alt: The summit station of the Zugspitze above Garmisch-Partenkirchen

places.tagline: Germany's highest mountain, and the World Cup slopes of the Kandahar.
places.intro: Where EverFlow began as a ski school. Garmisch-Partenkirchen lies below the Zugspitze, Germany's highest mountain at 2,962 m, with the Garmisch-Classic ski area right above the town.
facts: Ski coaching, families, a first ski week
places.who: Families, first-timers and anyone who wants coaching on varied terrain without a long transfer. The town hosted the 1936 Winter Olympics, and the Kandahar run is still on the World Cup calendar.
places.when: Winter for skiing, with the Zugspitze glacier often opening earlier and closing later than the slopes above the town. Summer for hiking, biking and the lakes.
places.how: About 1.5 hours by car from Munich Airport, or by train from Munich in around 1.5 hours. Innsbruck Airport is about an hour away.

places.name: Munich

image.alt: Marienplatz and the old town of Munich at sunset

places.tagline: The natural place for the first and last night of an alpine week.
places.intro: A city of museums, beer halls and Christmas markets. The mountains begin about an hour south of the city.
facts: About 1.5 hours by car to Garmisch-Partenkirchen
Arrival and departure days, culture, a city night before or after the snow
places.who: For guests who want a day of museums, beer halls or shopping before heading into the mountains, and for anyone who lands late and wants a good night's sleep before the drive.
places.when: All year. In winter a city night fits easily at the start or end of a ski week; the Christmas markets run through Advent.
places.how: Munich Airport has direct flights from across Europe and overseas. From the airport, the city centre is about 40 to 45 minutes by train or car.

places.name: Las Leñas

image.alt: The base of Las Leñas in the snow, below the peaks of the Andes

gallery.alt: Snow-covered peaks above Las Leñas under passing clouds
A chairlift at Las Leñas, with the snowy Andes behind
Snowy slopes and ridges at Las Leñas in the sun

places.tagline: Skiing high in the Andes of Mendoza, in the southern winter.
places.intro: Las Leñas lies in the Andes of Mendoza, with its base at 2,240 m and its top at 3,430 m. It is where our founder, Juan Rodrigo, grew up skiing.
facts: 80 km from Malargüe, 200 km from San Rafael, 1,200 km from Buenos Aires
From Buenos Aires to San Rafael and Mendoza, in winter
places.who: Skiers from Argentina, Brazil and beyond who want a ski week in the southern winter, high in the Andes.
places.when: The ski season runs from June to September inclusive.
places.how: In winter there are flights from Buenos Aires to San Rafael and Mendoza; from there by road to the valley, the last stretch on Ruta 222, where chains must be carried in winter. [laslenas.com](https://laslenas.com/)
